text:
Predicates:
SpillsFood(x) ::: x spills a lot of food on his clothing.
NotablyTidy(x) ::: x is notably tidy.
ClumsyFoodie(x) ::: x is a clumsy foodie who goes out frequently to find new food restaurants.
Cleanly(x) ::: x is cleanly.
ValuesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x values order and spotlessness.
PrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) ::: x's family prioritizes order and spotlessness.
Family(x, y) ::: x's family is y.
Premises:
∀x (SpillsFood(x) → ¬NotablyTidy(x)) ::: If people spill a lot of food on their clothing, then they are not notably tidy.
∀x (ClumsyFoodie(x) → SpillsFood(x)) ::: All clumsy foodies who go out frequently spill a lot of food.
∀x (Cleanly(x) → NotablyTidy(x)) ::: If people are cleanly, then they are notably tidy.
∀x (ValuesOrderAndSpotlessness(x) → Cleanly(x)) ::: If people value order and spotlessness, then they are cleanly.
∀x ∀y (Family(y, x) ∧ PrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(y) → ValuesOrderAndSpotlessness(y)) ::: All people whose families prioritize order and spotlessness value order and spotlessness.
Peter is either a person who spills a lot of food on his clothing and is cleanly, or a person who does not spill a lot of food on his clothing and is not cleanly ::: (SpillsFood(peter) ∧ Cleanly(peter)) ∨ (¬SpillsFood(peter) ∧ ¬Cleanly(peter))
Conclusion:
((ClumsyFoodie(peter) ∧ Family(familyOfPeter, x) ∧ PrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x)) ∨ (¬ClumsyFoodie(peter) ∧ ¬Family(familyOfPeter, x) ∧ ¬PrioritizesOrderAndSpotlessness(x)))
